exportResolved.note: Authoring forms the exporter resolves before the IR: rem → px (root font size), var() at the element, hsl()/hsla() → hex or rgba(), CSS-wide keywords → the inherited or initial value. Lint accepts them; the mapper never sees them and rejects them.

notes.handling: direct = written to USS (value validated); lowered = rewritten before mapping (by the Unity Lowering, or by the exporter: see the property's note); the mapper rejects leftovers; dropped = accepted and omitted; error = rejected with rule and fix. Properties not listed are U-CSS-023, value functions not listed are U-CSS-024.
notes.components: [min,max] space-separated components per list item (default [1,1]); list = comma separated list allowed
notes.dropValues: keyword values that are accepted and omitted
notes.loweredValues: keyword values valid only where the compiler lowers them (see the property's note); the mapper rejects them elsewhere
notes.loweredFunctions: value functions only the compiler consumes (see the property's note); the mapper rejects them elsewhere
notes.rejectedValues: keyword → {rule, fix}: values a dedicated lint rule rejects (e.g. display: grid is U-CSS-001); the mapper may report them with that rule and fix
notes.valueRule: a dedicated lint rule judges this property's values (U-CSS-023 checks neither its keywords nor its units)
notes.valueFix: the fix for any other rejected value of this property (rule U-CSS-023 unless valueRule names another)
notes.authoring: authoring-level overrides the lint applies because the exporter rewrites the value before the IR (handling, extra types or keywords, comma lists)
notes.lists: initialValues, svgPresentation, transformFunctions, keyframeProperties, timingKeywords, mediaFeatures, mediaTypes, layoutTransitionProperties, pseudoElements, pseudoClasses, atRules, elements, inputTypes and browserDefaults are read by the exporter's lint only
notes.typeUnits: the units of each value type the mapper's validation accepts (units lists the length and percent units)
notes.exportResolved: authoring forms the exporter resolves before the IR; see its note

filter.valueFix: Use only invert() in filter: it is the one filter function that matches Chromium at every viewport in the fidelity suite. blur(), contrast(), grayscale(), hue-rotate(), opacity() and sepia() exist in UI Toolkit but do not match yet; brightness(), saturate(), drop-shadow() and url() have no UI Toolkit equivalent. Bake the effect into an image instead.
filter.note: UI Toolkit 6000.3 filter functions: tint, opacity, invert, grayscale, sepia, blur, contrast, hue-rotate (and custom FilterFunctionDefinition assets); USS filter: fn(arg) …, % becomes a fraction, deg/rad/grad/turn radians, px stays px. functions lists the ones the fidelity suite measured to match at 2560, 1920 and 1280 (docs/findings/filters.md); the compiler writes each with its argument checked and explicit.
